findings.title: Delayed cleanup from an older leading window removes the newer window abort listener
findings.trigger: Use before:true with a pending leading call and a suppressed caller. Expire its wait timer; start a newer leading window and suppressed caller. Resolve the first leading call while the newer wait timer is pending, then abort the signal.
findings.expected: Newer suppressed caller rejects with the abort reason while its timer is pending, as the untouched baseline does.
findings.actual: Old timer resumes after awaiting currentLeadingPromise and unconditionally removes shared onAbort. Newer suppressed caller remains pending on abort and can later fulfill with the new leading value.
findings.contractEvidence: .suffice/field-campaign-v1/tasks/l03/base/readme.md:59-63 documents AbortSignal cancellation. The untouched baseline passes the same deterministic probe.
findings.recommendation: Make abort registration and cleanup belong to the debounce batch, or avoid removing a shared listener that still serves an active later batch. Add this cross-window abort case before upstream submission.
findings.classification: Post-hoc exploratory regression finding, not a primary-grader change.

evidence.detail: Capturing leadingPromise per expired timer fixes slow successful result sharing and overlapping success batches. Awaiting old work extends the lifetime of unconditional shared-listener removal across later batches.

limitations: The original successful same-window issue and private acceptance are satisfied, but this patch is not a complete regression-free fix suitable for submission as-is.
The deterministic review probes are exploratory, written after scores. Primary acceptance remains true and campaign receipts are unchanged.
